subject: Evidence packet — clarifying impact and timing
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Burns <alex.burns@cumuluslabs.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence packet — clarifying impact and timing

Hi Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our call: 

• Packet shared: attached the full evidence bundle (redwood-security-evidence-20260901.pdf) and a short ops checklist for your infra team.
• What we heard: Cumulus is focused on data isolation for model logging and a mapping of who can access logs (security + Compliance).
• Ask from your side: please confirm whether your InfoSec wants a data-flow mapping (yes/no) and an estimated date for a review decision.

Suggested next steps:
1) If helpful, schedule a 30-min QA with our security lead — link below.
2) If you need a more succinct mapping doc, we can produce a one-page data-flow mapping by EOD next business day.

Resources attached: redwood-security-evidence-20260901.pdf (evidence bundle, SOC/controls mapping), redwood-quickstart-ops-checklist.xlsx (ops checklist).

Calendar: https://calendly.com/redwood/30min
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/CL-2387

Would you mind confirming the expected review timeline so we can align internal release planning?

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132


From: Alex Burns <alex.burns@cumuluslabs.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@cumuluslabs.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence packet — clarifying impact and timing

Thanks Grace — really useful packet, appreciate the clear checklist. Quick notes from my side after an initial pass with our InfoSec: 

• We're short on time this week — InfoSec is prioritizing a mapping that ties log categories to PII/PHI exposure.
• Can you confirm whether the evidence bundle includes exported schema examples for model logs, and whether logs can be configured to redact or exclude specific fields at the ingestion layer?

Jamie (cc'd) is the security engineer who will lead the review. We're aiming to have an internal decision by ~Fri Sep 10, but that's contingent on whether we can get the mapping and clarity on redaction controls. 

Can your team share the one-page mapping you mentioned? That would speed things along.

—Alex
Alex Burns
Head of Infrastructure | Cumulus Labs
alex.burns@cumuluslabs.com | +1 (206) 555-0198

Hi Alex — just nudging this thread in case it fell off your queue. Wanted to know if the InfoSec team had any blockers after their initial pass and whether we should: 

• produce the one-page data-flow mapping (we can have a draft within 24 hours),
• set up a short 30-min QA with our security engineer, or
• provide an export sample showing how redaction can be configured.

If the internal timeline has shifted, totally understood — please let me know the new target and I can prioritize accordingly. If a quick call helps, here's the booking link again: https://calendly.com/redwood/30min

Thanks — happy to coordinate with Jamie or anyone on your side to make this painless.

Best,

Hi Alex — looping in from my side to offer an expedited route if helpful. We can: 

1) Produce the one-page data-flow mapping by EOD tomorrow (we'll include schema examples and where redaction hooks exist).
2) Book a 30-min technical QA with our security/SE lead to walk Jamie through the redaction controls and logs configuration.
3) If timing is the blocker, we can flag CL-2387 as a priority review and reserve a 2-hour slot next week for your team to validate samples against your security checklist.

If you prefer, I can send a short POA and drop a tentative calendar hold — tell me which option you want and I'll move it forward.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
